title: The Tax Crackdown Isn’t Over
text:
The Tax Crackdown Isn’t Over

Christopher Beddor, Ernan Cui, Wei He

Gavekal Dragonomics | 18 Nov 2026

For the last few months, taxes have been the talk of Hong Kong’s financial sector. Mainland residents had until October 22 to declare and pay sometimes years of back taxes on their offshore trusts, vehicles company founders have long used in part to shield holdings in offshore-listed firms—at least until the government declared them subject to tax after all.Last week, the State Taxation Administration said the crackdown had led to the declaration of more than RMB160bn in income taxes, of which at least RMB120bn was paid in October. That’s a big enough sum to make October 2026 the biggest month of income-tax collection in China’s history, and probably exacerbated Hong Kong’s stock-market decline as some taxpayers sold shares to pay their bills.
